replies:
Three focused prep pieces you can use in the room, plus two practice questions to answer aloud. I assumed you want concise, interview-ready phrasing for an M&A/valuation analyst final round. If any fact I use below (school, current employer, years) is wrong, tell me the single correction and I’ll update.

1) 60‑second "Tell me about yourself" (analyst version) — use this as the backbone, fill brackets with your facts, keep it ~50–60s:
"I’m [Name]. I studied [Major] at [School]. For the past [X years/months] I’ve worked at [Current/most recent employer] doing financial modeling and transaction support, where I built and maintained [number] DCF/LBO/merger models, led diligence on [type/size of engagements], and produced client-ready materials that directly supported [result—e.g., a closed deal or a recommended price range]. I’m strongest in accounting linkages, Excel modeling and translating model outputs into clear recommendations for partners. I’m excited about this role at Lincoln because of its focus on [pick one: mid-market M&A / cross-border deals / sector focus that matches you], and I want to take on more ownership
of end-to-end deal execution."

2) Three short STAR stories to have memorized (one line situation + your action + metric/result you will add)
- Team win: "Led the financial model update for a sell-side pitch on a 48-hour turnaround; I consolidated multiple analysts’ work, fixed linkage errors, and the model was used in the pitch that increased auction participation and drove a stronger final bid." (add exact numbers)
- Hard problem: "On a carve-out where public comps were scarce, I rebuilt pro forma operating metrics from segment disclosures and adjusted EBITDA bridges, narrowing valuation ranges and enabling a clearer pricing recommendation." (add % or $ impact)
- Failure/learning: "Early on I missed a tax timing adjustment that affected near-term cash flow; I owned it, re-ran scenarios, implemented a tax/timing checklist in our model build, and it prevented similar mistakes on subsequent deals." (add what changed, e.g., 'reduced errors by X%')

Prep each to state: situation, your specific actions (what you did, tools or analyses used), and a quantified outcome.
3) Quick technical refresh — practice these aloud, 90–120s answers with a short numeric example where possible
- Accounting linkage: "Walk me through the three statements and how a $X change flows." (Show IS → NI → CFS adjustments → BS link; explain non‑cash addbacks, working capital, debt changes.)
- DCF build and sensitivities: "How do you build a DCF and choose terminal value method?" (Forecast FCFs, compute WACC, terminal via growth or exit multiple—explain when each is appropriate—and show why WACC/growth sensitivity matters; give a one-line WACC calc.)
- Transaction mechanics: "Walk me through an accretion/dilution test." (Explain pro forma EPS, deal financing mix, synergies, and what makes a deal accretive immediately vs. over time; give a simple before/after EPS example.)

Two behavioral practice questions — answer them aloud, then paste your answers here and I’ll score and edit them:

1) "Why Lincoln International? Why this team?" — target: two sentences: one firm-specific reason (sector/mid-market/cross-border) + one personal fit (type of deal, ownership level, what you want to learn).
2) "Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate." — use STAR, emphasize how you used data or structure to resolve it and the learning.
Pre-interview checklist (do these before the call)
- Confirm time, time zone, meeting link and who’s on the panel.
- Print one-page cheat sheet: three stories and Top 5 technical bullets (accounting linkages, DCF steps, accretion/dilution, working capital, common model checks).
- Test audio/video and screen share; close unrelated tabs and notifications.
- Have laptop, charger, and a pen; keep pacing so answers stay under 2 minutes for technical and ~60s for the opener.
Next step I’ll do for you
Run a timed mock now: say "mock me for Analyst at Lincoln International" and I’ll ask the first question. Or paste your answers to the two behavioral practice questions and I’ll score and rewrite them for the room.

One question: do you want the mock focused heavier on technical modeling or on behavioral/fit?

replies:
You don't have any application on file yet. The one step that starts this is: pick the posting you want me to prepare an application for (paste its link or job listing text, or tell me which of the jobs I previously showed you you mean).

Assuming a standard online ATS form, here is exactly what I will fill and show you, field by field, for the first application card I prepare (I assume resume + short cover letter; I will default persona to "base" unless you ask otherwise):
1) Employer name — the company name exactly as the posting states.
2) Job title — the exact title from the posting.
3) Location — city / remote / on-site as the posting lists it.
4) Link to posting — the posting URL or the exact posting text you pasted.
5) Resume file — the PDF resume I will attach (made only from your confirmed facts). I will state the filename and provide a private 7-day link to that PDF. If you haven't given name/email for the resume header, I will ask before building it.
6) Which resume persona is used — 'base' or a named persona you chose; default is 'base'.
7) Cover letter — a tailored cover letter (≤400 words) with [brackets] for any missing specifics (hiring manager name, exact metric). I will show the full draft for you to edit or approve.
8) Application form answers — each question from the form and my suggested answer shown verbatim (including checkbox/yes-no choices). I will flag any screening/knockout questions and show the best truthful answer.
9) Salary expectations / current compensation — the exact text I will enter, or “not listed” if you prefer not to answer; I will not invent numbers.
10) Work authorization — the exact option I will pick (e.g., “Authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship”) only after you tell me; otherwise I will leave it blank and ask.
11) Earliest start date — the date or timeframe I will enter, using what you tell me or left as [earliest start date].
12) Attachments — list of files attached (resume, cover letter, portfolio, certifications) with filenames; I attach only files you explicitly approve.
13) Referral / source — the field that says how you found the job; I will set it to “Trainee” / “job board” / “employee referral: [name]” exactly as you provide.
14) Additional notes / message to recruiter — an optional 1–3 sentence message I will draft (≤120 words if an email). I will show it for your edit/approval.
15) Applicant screening responses — answers to screening questions (background check, convictions, eligibility). I will show each required true/false and flag anything that could be a knockout.
16) Privacy / consent checkboxes — I will note which boxes must be checked; you must confirm them before submission.
17) Final preview — a single preview showing every field as it will be submitted, attachments listed, and any flagged risk (knockouts, missing required docs).
18) Action note — I will state the exact next step I will take after your approval: either queue the application for your browser extension to submit, or prepare an email for you to send from your connected mail. Nothing gets sent without your approval and the appropriate connection running.

Assumptions I made: one standard online ATS form; you want both a resume and a short cover letter attached; your mail is not connected so I will queue rather than send email unless you connect it. If any of these are wrong, tell me and I’ll adjust the defaults.
Next step: paste the posting link or the posting text for the single job you want me to prepare, or say “use the first posting you showed me” if that’s the one — then I’ll prepare the exact card and show every filled field for your approval.

One question: do you want me to include a short tailored cover letter by default, or attach only a resume?
